title: A Gaussian activation bound excludes several saved mouse visual spectra under equal image variance
abstract: We tested whether pointwise activation of equal-variance Gaussian image features can reproduce saved mouse visual response spectra. We derived a necessary bound for every activation with finite Gaussian second moment, including the variance removed by image centering. If p is the normalized input spectrum and q is the centered output spectrum, their cumulative shares must obey (1 - sum p squared) F_q(k) <= F_p(k). A four-image square-activation example attains the centering bound. With saved VISp spectra as inputs, four of five higher cortical mean profiles fail in both Neuropixels and two-photon aggregate results. For VISam, required removed variance shares are 0.0971 and 0.6035, above allowed shares 0.0392 and 0.0341. Numerical checks use 300 nonstationary covariance matrices and 200,000 Gaussian features. This is a conditional model test on saved covariance surrogates. Equal image variance and Gaussian features are untested, and there are no new mouse-level intervals. Independent VISp draw comparisons also show sampling sensitivity. The result constrains a specific activation class but does not identify a cortical mechanism.

display.caption: The required centering loss exceeds the Gaussian activation bound for several saved profiles. A synthetic pooling control can exceed this bound. These are conditional model comparisons, with no animal confidence intervals.
